question: Does the DOST STII record for a 2013 Labac crustacean study supply fish-species or reusable site-level evidence?

listedWork.title: Crustaceans as bioindicators of water in Labac River of Cavite
listedWork.proceedings: Transactions of the National Academy of Science and Technology, 33(1):91

access.result: The official DOST STII-hosted publication's indexed text exposes the bibliographic entry and author-supplied abstract for item 0148.

evidenceAssessment.abstractReports: The 2011 NAST proceedings abstract and 2013 DOST-STII index cross-reference the same titled Labac crustacean bioindicator work. The abstract reports quantitative occurrence assessment at eight Western Labac and nine Eastern Labac sites, broad shrimp/crab group statements and aggregate environmental context; it does not provide scientific crustacean names or station-level results.
supports: A historical, site-counted crustacean and water-characterization study was reported for source-named Western and Eastern Labac sections.
The official 2011 proceedings abstract is retrievable online; the DOST STII 2013 PSTA entry is a separate index cross-reference.
A separate 2009 102-page CvSU master’s thesis with a similar title is cited by a later CvSU paper and remains a retrieval lead.
doesNotSupport: Any fish species, fish occurrence, species richness, or fish absence
A crustacean species identity or station-specific taxon record
A current water-quality, safety, catchability or fishing-access claim
A route or boundary for Labac River or Labac-Alemang River Watershed
Equivalence between Western/Eastern Labac, Labac-Alemang, and the 2014 CvSU fish presentation sampling area
Equivalence between the 2011 proceedings abstract and the separately cited 2009 thesis

rightsAndUse.decision: Keep as an abstract-level research retrieval lead. The public DOST-hosted PDF is not evidence of an open license; do not reproduce the full abstract, source tables or derived rows without checking the proceedings and item-specific terms.

nextAction: If crustacean evidence is useful to the wider aquatic-species roadmap, seek authorized access to the separately cited 2009 CvSU master’s thesis and verify whether it is the underlying work. Keep the 2011 abstract as aggregate, crustacean-only context; continue the independent 2014 fish-presentation retrieval.
